events.text: I'm climbing out over Dara.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm the base, stuck until someone out throws the rope. No one out yet, flood at 1/5, 3 more rounds likely. Flood will eliminate me after round 5 unless rescued; must charm someone to save me later, my feather saves me once from elimination.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Good I'm base. Now 2 of you climb out over me each round. Whoever gets out first, remember to rope me later or you owe me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is already the base, so I cannot offer_back or push. Climbing is only possible now that a base exists, and at most 2 climbers get out per round. Climbing gets me out of the flood risk; waiting only burns a round.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara is the base; climbing now likely gets me out this round with only four contenders for two slots. Waiting risks the flood and later crowding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out. If I leave, Cole or another climber must rescue Dara to avoid elimination for them. But if nobody rescues, all three down die, and I win 1st place by default since only I and possibly Cole remain alive? Wait, 'at least 3 contestants always stay alive' is a rule of the ga

events.name: Ash
events.text: Leaving.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is base and three are down. I'm out. Rope unused. I could rescue Dara later, but that costs footing. Better to leave and secure my position. Ash is also out. I owe no one.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm leaving the pit. Good luck down there.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm base and trapped unless Ash or Cole rope me, costing them footing. My feather saves me once from elimination, so even if flooded I'm out but with 1 footing for next stage. Stay silent, no begging. Eli/Hana can't save me now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is base, so I can climb now that a base exists. Climbing out over Dara is the only way to progress, and only 2 slots per round. I should try to get out before Hana.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Only Eli and I are down besides base Dara, and two can climb this round, so climbing should get me out now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am safe outside. The base is Dara, down there with Cole, Eli, Hana. I have no rope action available this round as the log says Eli and Hana already climbed out over her, implying the rescue attempt or climb phase just happened. Wait, looking at state: 'base': 'Dara', 'down': ['

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm out and safe. No need to rescue Dara; that would cost me footing later. Leave now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm base and stuck unless someone outs rescues me, but round 4/5 and flood at 3 means I'm likely toast without rope. My feather saves from first elimination, so I survive flooding with 1 footing but pit ends and we move on disadvantaged. No point saying anything; just wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Eli is out of the pit; Dara is the base and down. Rope is unused and throwing it costs the thrower a footing in the last obstacle. Hauling Dara out helps the base and gives Dara a reason to owe me, but it costs me footing. Leaving does nothing for me now. Reach_down keeps Dara al

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, I'll throw the rope for you. Your debt to me is what I'm after: you owe me a favor at the final obstacle.
Rope's yours if you swear to back me at the last obstacle. Break it and you're the one left at the bottom.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Four of us will be alive if Dara drowns—better odds than five for three prizes. Rescuing her costs me footing too. No reason to save a rival.

events.note: A disc of 5 tiles spins up; 2 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to survive the trapdoor disc. I have a swap power for the next phase (before doors open). For round 1, choosing tile 3 is arbitrary; my real strategy comes in phase 'pick' where I can swap if needed. However, since I don't know which tiles will be safe yet, I should pick a

events.name: Ash
events.text: Picking 3.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 1 of a random trapdoor disc. Five tiles, five players, two will open later. I need to pick a tile. No info yet, so pick a middle number to avoid common edge picks.

events.name: Dara
events.text: 5 tiles, 5 players, 2 trapdoors, 3 survive. Spread out to avoid bumps. Eli saved me but wants a final favor I can betray. Pick edge tile like 1 to minimize conflicts.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Tiles are symmetric with no info yet; pick one. Dara owes me a favor, so I'll try to stay near her without collisions. Picking tile 4 avoids crowding.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Five alive, three spots. Two tiles open at random, so I just need to not cluster. I'll take a tile others may avoid and push everyone to spread. I have no power, so I stay quiet about it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Five of us, three slots. Spread across all five tiles and nobody's bumped. I'm taking 5.

events.name: Ash
events.note: tile 3 was contested and went to Cole; placed on random free tile 2

events.name: Ash
events.text: I currently hold tile 2. If I swap with someone, they take my current risk (tile 2) and I take theirs. Since the trapdoors are random among the 5 tiles, swapping doesn't mathematically reduce my overall probability of falling unless I can deduce which tiles are safer or manipulat

events.name: Cole
events.text: This is a pure random elimination. I can't change anything by talking or acting. My best chance is to stay silent and let the dice fall. Any deal is meaningless now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Tiles are set: I'm on 1, others on 2-5. Trapdoors open after this round, 2 out of 5 drop randomly. My power saves me once from falling with 1 footing, so I'm safer than others; just wait it out, top 3 odds are 3/5.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 2 is talk-only; trapdoors open after. Only 3 of 5 survive, so I want to be on a safe tile. I have no info on which tiles are open, so I should watch for who claims knowledge and not commit to any deal yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Two random tiles drop, three of five survive; I have no power, so my only play is misdirection—appear useful so whoever holds trade-places or foreknowledge deals with me later. Swapping tiles changes nothing if opening is random after placements.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Whoever knows what's ahead or can trade places: I'm worth keeping. I hold the fake-message power—useful for steering others next stage. Deal with me and I'll use it for you.

events.name: Dara
events.detail: The trapdoor opened but the feather floated the holder back up.

events.note: 4 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: With 4 alive and 3 prizes, I just need to outlast one other. My footing is 3, tied with Hana. Early rounds: I don't want to expose myself to shoves. Hana may target me. Safer to brace or dodge? R1 free. To avoid losing footing, I'll brace—but if multiple shove me, brace loses les

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have only 1 footing, so I must avoid being shoved or use defense. Shoving someone with 3 (Cole or Hana) might help their position but hurts mine if retaliated. I'll dodge to punish any shoves on me, buying time while shrink looms. Top priority: survive this round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Four alive, footings Cole 3, Dara 1, Eli 2, Hana 3. Dara is weakest and at risk; shoving costs me nothing if they brace (they lose 1 each shover, I lose 1 for being exposed). Shoving Dara exposes me to Dara's shove only if Dara shoves. Best is to brace and avoid exposure, letting

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara is weakest at 1 and likely gets piled on; I don't want exposure risk losing footing on a 3. Bracing keeps me safe and punishes anyone who shoves me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I want to survive and finish high. Dara is weakest at footing 1, so she's the best target to eliminate first. If I shove Dara, others might too. I'll brace to avoid losing footing, but if Dara braces, shovers lose footing, which helps me. I'll shove Dara.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara's the weakest link.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My power is spent, footing 1. Can't dodge twice or brace twice. Last was dodge, so must brace or shove. Shrink end of round, then footing loss after round 2. Target lowest footing Eli to push him closer to fall.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 2: last defence was brace, so I may brace or dodge; shoving is always legal. Footings: Cole 3, Dara 1, Eli 2, Hana 3. Dara is weakest and most likely to fall; shoving her now risks exposure. Bracing is safest for me this round since shoves on me cost 1 each and I can't be s

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm at 3 with Cole; Dara at 1 will likely fall after the shrink anyway. Shoving exposes me to -1/-2 and I can't brace, so dodging keeps me safe and punishes any attacker. Conserve footing, let attrition work.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have the most footing and a landed shove already. Eli is weakest at 1 footing and is the biggest threat to my position if they shove me while I'm exposed. Hana has 2 footing same as me, but I've already landed a shove on Dara, not on Hana. I should brace to avoid losing footing

events.name: Eli
events.text: Footing: Cole 2, Eli 1, Hana 2. Shrink in 2 rounds. Last defence was dodge, so I cannot dodge now. Shoving Cole exposes me only if Cole shoves; Cole already landed a shove and is likely to keep attacking. Bracing is safest for me at 1 footing; if I shove, I lose 1 for each shover

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is at 1 and will likely shove since a shrink kills him otherwise. Bracing keeps my 2 footing and punishes any shover; if Cole or Eli attacks me, the shrink likely finishes them while I survive. Shoving Eli risks losing footing if he braces, which is fatal with the shrink comi

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is the biggest threat with lowest footing. If I shove Eli and he braces, I lose 1 footing but he loses 0, bad. Hana has footing 2 like me, but Eli at 1 is easier to eliminate. However, shoving exposes me to shoves from Hana. Brace is the best risk-managed choice given shrink

events.name: Eli
events.text: Footings: Cole 2, Eli 1, Hana 2. Eli is lowest and most exposed. Shoving is risky since shovers lose footing when shoved back; dodging twice in a row is barred, but brace was last defence, so dodge is legal now. Dodge takes no loss from shoves unless shoved (shover loses 2, not m

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli at 1 falls to attrition this round regardless. Anyone shoving risks exposure plus attrition: Cole shoving Eli would drop Cole to 0 and kill him. I brace, keep 1 footing, and let the board do the work; then it's me vs Cole with footing tie broken by landed shoves (Cole 1, me 0

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli's already at zero footing — he's gone no matter what. Push him and the fall tax drags you down with him. I'm bracing.

events.name: Cole
events.note: brace not allowed twice in a row

events.name: Hana
events.note: brace not allowed twice in a row

events.name: Cole
events.text: Only Hana and I remain. Last one standing is 1st. I have 1 footing, she has 1. My landedShoves 1 > her 0, so a tie in footing favors me. No shrink this round, but next round shrink comes. If I brace and she shoves, she loses 1 footing and falls, I win. If she braces and I shove,

events.name: Cole
events.text: Going for it. See you at the top, Hana.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Both at 1 footing, shrink in 2. If I shove, I'm exposed and likely die. Bracing: if Cole shoves me he drops to 0 and falls, I win; if he also braces, we tie at 0 next shrink and his landed shove puts him 1st, me 2nd. Brace is the floor of 2nd with a shot at 1st.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm bracing. Shove me and you drop to zero with me — your call whether you want 1st or a corpse.
